source.title: Tracing the Thoughts of a Large Language Model

page_placements.theme: Latent multi-hop and intermediate computation within one forward pass

record.file_problem: Full blog post is present. It summarizes linked papers, whose full methods and case-study details are not included here.
record.tranche_reason: Reports causal-intervention results bearing on the claim, but as a summary of linked work rather than an independent replication; the detailed protocol is not given.
record.gate_note: The post reports rhyme-planning observations and intervention outcomes, plus a multi-step-reasoning intervention. Other case studies in the post do not bear on the listed versions. Results cited or discussed in comments are not treated as study results.
record.test_reason: This is Anthropic's companion blog post for 'On the Biology of a Large Language Model', an original source. It restates that paper's own rhyme-planning interventions on Claude 3.5 Haiku. It reports results bearing on V1, but it is not an independent test, so no verdicts are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also say they set out to show the model did not plan ahead and found that it did. They claim Claude plans 'many words ahead', though they show this only for a two-line couplet. Their caveat that the method captures only a fraction of the computation and may introduce artifacts is reported correctly.
record.recipe_differences: The post describes suppressing or injecting concepts and swapping intermediate concepts, but omits the detailed method and protocol provided in the linked papers.
record.method_sensitivity: The injected concept changes the outcome: suppressing “rabbit” yields “habit”, while injecting “green” yields a non-rhyming ending.

fits_no_version.finding: Swapping intermediate 'Texas' features for 'California' changes the answer from Austin to Sacramento in Claude 3.5 Haiku.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models perform latent multi-hop reasoning through causally used intermediate entity representations within one forward pass.

record.problems: The post gives illustrative examples rather than quantitative results, with no uncertainty estimates or controls. It identifies Claude 3.5 Haiku but does not state its size or training stage. The authors note that the method captures only a fraction of computation and may produce artifacts.

untested.parts: Not tested: no decoding of future tokens from a single hidden state.
Not tested: there is no test of why features are computed (for later positions versus as a next-token side effect).
Not tested: no open-weight models or open tools are used.
Not tested: no look-ahead in other tasks such as chess or Sokoban; the multi-hop example is not future-token planning.
Not tested: no test of planning depth or of heuristic explanations.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given because this post restates results from an original source (Biology of a LLM) by the same team. Results cited in comments, such as Olah's 'an astronomer' example, are not study results. All evidence is illustrative and single-example, with no quantitative measures.

versions.untested_parts: Only the described Claude 3.5 Haiku poetry example is covered; other frontier models, prompts, and rhyme settings are not reported.
The post does not test whether a single hidden state predicts tokens several positions ahead.
The post shows causal use of an earlier rhyme concept, but does not establish why the feature is computed or distinguish that explanation from all next-token-prediction side effects.
No smaller open-weight models or open attribution-graph or probing tools are tested.
A multi-step reasoning example is described; chess, Sokoban, and other architectures are not tested.
The post does not test whether planning is shallow, incidental, or merely heuristic.

rows.subject: Claude 3.5 Haiku
rows.operation_detail: Trace the model's rhyme-planning activity before it begins the second line.

conditions.value: rhyming poem; second line follows a line ending in “grab it”

rows.measure: Whether a candidate rhyme is represented before the second line is written
rows.value: The model plans “rabbit” before starting the second line.
rows.note: The post describes this as planning ahead; it gives no quantitative measure of the representation.
rows.check: Drop the V3 link. The post shows candidate rhymes are represented before the line, but it does not test whether features are computed because they help later positions.
